description: DCC operators monitor 74 substations and about 1,900 field devices and operate breakers, reclosers, and capacitor banks through SCADA
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Without SCADA, every switching step needs a crew at the device; restoration slows and switching errors endanger crews. 4 h is the longest the DCC can run on crews and radio in normal weather (2 h during a declared storm). Continuous replication to the hot standby gives near-zero loss for real-time data; RPO 1 h covers database and display changes made since the last replicated configuration snapshot
manual_workaround: Station crews dispatched to the 20 largest substations; switching by radio from the DCC; paper operator log
dependent_third_parties: SCADA and ADMS vendor; fiber, licensed radio, and private LTE carriers
dependent_people_or_facilities: 28 system operators and 6 shift supervisors; DCC and backup DCC; substation crews
quantified_operational_impact: About 60 crews needed at substations within 2 h; each switching step takes about 30 minutes by crew instead of seconds; restoration of a feeder lockout slows from about 5 minutes to about 60 minutes
quantified_regulatory_impact: Loss of SCADA with a cyber cause can trigger DOE-417 criterion 3 within 1 hour; EOP-004-4 report if a BES Emergency causes an uncontrolled loss of 200 MW or more of firm load for 15 minutes or more
public_and_crew_safety_impact: Severe: crews switch under time pressure; risk of energizing a line under clearance if status is wrong

description: OMS predicts outage locations from calls, AMI, and SCADA events and dispatches crews
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Restoration slows sharply without outage prediction; in a declared storm the MTD drops to 4 h because thousands of outages must be grouped. Managed database point-in-time restore gives a 1 h RPO; the 2026-05-19 restore test took 3 h 10 min
manual_workaround: Paper trouble tickets; dispatch by radio; outage map built from contact center logs
dependent_systems: SYS-02; SYS-09 operations workloads account; SYS-11; SYS-05; SYS-06
dependent_third_parties: Cloud provider; SCADA and ADMS vendor (OMS module support); cellular carrier
quantified_operational_impact: Average outage duration rises by about 40% without OMS grouping; in a hurricane, restoration of the last 10% of customers can slip by 1 to 2 days
quantified_regulatory_impact: Restoration duties and storm reporting to the state public service commission (outside this cyber analysis); DOE-417 criterion 12 if more than 50,000 customers are out for 1 hour or more
public_and_crew_safety_impact: Moderate: crews may be sent to the wrong location or into hazards that the OMS would have flagged

business_process: BES line protection at Substations N, E, L, and H
description: 26 relays protect the 230 kV and 115 kV BES line terminals; protection staff maintain settings and test under PRC-005
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Relays run locally and keep protecting if SCADA or remote access is lost. If relay integrity is in doubt after a cyber event, the transmission owner may take the line out of service; restoring approved settings and testing takes about 8 h per substation with two crews. RPO 0: the last approved settings file is the recovery point
manual_workaround: Transmission owner operates with the line out of service; protection staff reload approved settings on site
dependent_systems: SYS-04; relay engineering workstations; settings file server
dependent_third_parties: Transmission Owners A and B; relay testing contractor
dependent_people_or_facilities: 22 protection engineers and technicians; Substations N, E, L, and H
quantified_operational_impact: A doubtful relay can take a 230 kV or 115 kV line out of service; with one line out, Substations N and E lose redundancy for about 180,000 customers
quantified_regulatory_impact: CIP-003-9 Attachment 1 Section 4 incident response; possible Reportable Cyber Security Incident (E-ISAC notice) and DOE-417 criterion 2 within 1 hour
public_and_crew_safety_impact: Severe: a protection misoperation can damage equipment or extend an outage across a substation

description: Switching orders are written, approved, and executed, and clearance tags protect crews working on de-energized lines, through the OMS switching module
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Crew safety drives this process. Paper switching orders work but are slow and error-prone; after 4 h, planned work must stop. The switching module writes each step to the managed database; RPO 15 minutes keeps the status of open clearances recoverable
manual_workaround: Printed switching orders and clearance log at the DCC; read-back by radio; no new planned outages until the module is restored
dependent_third_parties: Cloud provider; SCADA and ADMS vendor
quantified_operational_impact: About 70 switching orders a day; paper processing takes about 3 times longer; planned work for about 40 crews stops after 4 h
quantified_regulatory_impact: OSHA electrical safety rules for clearances apply (not assessed here); an injury would trigger regulatory investigation
public_and_crew_safety_impact: Severe: a lost or wrong clearance status can energize a line where a crew is working

business_process: Customer contact center, IVR, and portal
description: Customers report outages and handle accounts by phone, IVR, and the portal
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Outage calls feed the OMS; call volume rises from about 9,000 to as many as 90,000 a day in a hurricane. Vendor SaaS with a 1 h RPO
manual_workaround: Recorded outage message; overflow to the storm call vendor; manual call logging
dependent_third_parties: CIS vendor; contact center platform vendor; phone carrier; storm call vendor
quantified_operational_impact: About 9,000 calls a day; each hour down leaves about 375 callers without service; storm overflow vendor costs about $3,000 an hour
quantified_regulatory_impact: None directly; complaints to the state public service commission rise
public_and_crew_safety_impact: Moderate: customers cannot report hazards such as downed lines (911 remains available)

description: Collect interval reads, outage and restoration events, and remote connect and disconnect for the company and the 4 client utilities
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Meters store interval data for weeks, so reads are not lost. About 900 remote connects and disconnects a day must go to field staff, at about $45 per truck visit
manual_workaround: Field connects and disconnects; estimated reads
quantified_operational_impact: About 900 remote orders a day become truck visits; outage events from meters stop flowing to the OMS
quantified_regulatory_impact: Contract service levels for the 4 client utilities (meter data delivery)

description: Bill calculation, printing, and payment posting for about 265,000 accounts in 21 daily bill cycles
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Bills run in daily cycles; a 3-day delay is recoverable with overtime. About $1.63 million of billing is delayed for each day of outage. Payments continue through the processor
manual_workaround: Delay bill cycles; payments continue through the processor hosted page and IVR service
dependent_third_parties: CIS vendor; payment processor; bill print vendor
quantified_operational_impact: About $4.9 million of billing delayed at the MTD (cash, not lost revenue); about 12,500 bills a day held
quantified_regulatory_impact: State tariff and billing rules on bill timing (not assessed here)

business_process: Contract services for the 4 client utilities
description: Billing, CIS hosting, after-hours outage calls, and meter data management for 2 municipal utilities and 2 cooperatives (about 58,000 meters)
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Client contracts set a 1-business-day billing service level and 99.5% monthly contact center availability, with a 5% monthly fee credit for each missed level (about $58,000 per client per miss). Losing a client would cost about $3.5 million a year in fees
manual_workaround: Clients bill from prior-month estimates; after-hours calls roll to each client duty officer
dependent_systems: SYS-06; SYS-05; SYS-08; SYS-09 analytics account
dependent_third_parties: CIS vendor; AMI vendor; contact center platform vendor
quantified_operational_impact: Up to 4 clients miss billing and call service levels; about 2,000 client bills a day held
quantified_regulatory_impact: The company is a third-party agent of the clients for Fla. Stat. 501.171 purposes; client contracts require security incident notice within 48 hours

business_process: Wholesale power scheduling and load forecasting
description: Daily day-ahead schedule and 7-day forecast sent to the wholesale supplier; solar PPA output forecast
process_owner: Director of Power Supply and Rates
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: The supplier needs a schedule each morning. A missed or poor schedule costs about $150,000 on a normal day and up to $1.2 million on a peak day. The supplier can reuse the prior day schedule
manual_workaround: Reuse the prior day schedule adjusted for weather; the supplier forecast
dependent_systems: SYS-15 (AI-001); SYS-09 analytics account; SYS-01 historian replica
dependent_third_parties: Wholesale power supplier; weather data provider; solar PPA counterparty
dependent_people_or_facilities: Lead Load Forecasting Analyst; data analyst; Director of Power Supply and Rates
quantified_operational_impact: One day of schedules at risk; on a peak day the cost reaches $1.2 million
public_and_crew_safety_impact: Minimal (indirect: an under-forecast can leave a substation near its limit, see P10)

description: Open move-in accounts, verify identity, obtain consumer reports, set deposits, and handle identity theft red flags
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: About 1,100 move-ins a day. Service can be connected with a pending deposit decision for up to 3 days under the credit procedure
manual_workaround: Connect service with deposit decision pending; manual identity checks on paper
quantified_operational_impact: About 3,300 move-ins processed without a deposit decision at the MTD
quantified_regulatory_impact: Identity Theft Prevention Program procedures must still run (16 CFR 681.1(d)); FCRA adverse action notices for deposits

business_process: Field work management and mobile workforce
description: Work orders, crew assignments, maps, and switching steps on 310 truck tablets
process_owner: Vice President of Operations and Field Services
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Crews can work from paper work packs for a day; after that, crew productivity drops by about a third
manual_workaround: Printed work packs; radio dispatch; paper maps
dependent_systems: SYS-11; SYS-02; SYS-09 operations workloads account
quantified_operational_impact: About 110 crews lose digital work orders and maps; productivity loss about $80,000 a day
public_and_crew_safety_impact: Moderate: crews lose map hazard layers on the tablets

description: Design work, GIS updates, and protection studies
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Work can be deferred; GIS changes are low volume
quantified_operational_impact: Design backlog grows by about 5 days of work

description: Automatic fault location, isolation, and service restoration on 40 pilot feeders
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: If the FLISR module is down, the 40 pilot feeders revert to manual restoration through SCADA. The pilot carries no regulatory duty today
manual_workaround: Disable FLISR; operators restore the 40 feeders manually through SCADA
quantified_operational_impact: Outages on 40 feeders (about 38,000 customers) take about 45 minutes longer to restore
quantified_regulatory_impact: None today; the planned adaptive load-shedding module would be a medium impact BES Cyber System (P03)

description: Email, chat, files, and video calls for coordination
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Storm coordination relies on chat and email, but radio and phones cover critical coordination
manual_workaround: Phones, text messages, and radio; printed storm contact lists
dependent_third_parties: Productivity suite vendor; identity provider vendor
quantified_operational_impact: About 850 staff slowed; storm coordination falls back to phones

description: Time capture, payroll, onboarding, and terminations
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Payroll runs biweekly; missing it has legal and morale impact
manual_workaround: Repeat the prior payroll through the payroll provider
quantified_operational_impact: One payroll for 850 staff at risk

description: General ledger, purchasing, vendor payments, and the wholesale power invoice
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: The wholesale power invoice is paid monthly; a 5-day delay is manageable with the supplier
manual_workaround: Manual payments for critical vendors; delayed close
quantified_operational_impact: Month-end close slips by up to 5 days
